record.title: Poipet security barricades selectively block access to the Thailand crossing
record.region: East and Southeast Asia and Oceania
record.scope: Access to Poipet international crossing via barricades on National Road 5
record.direction: Observed outbound access from Cambodia; no blanket bidirectional closure inferred.
record.movement: Cambodian traders and residents seeking to reach the Thai market; vehicles. Tourists and casino workers initially delayed.
record.exceptions: Casino workers were allowed past the barricades toward casinos around 08:30; this does not establish their passage across the international boundary. Foreign tourists were subsequently allowed to cross the border. Other local traders and vehicles remained blocked when reported.
record.enforcement: On-site reporting, photographs and interviews establish multiple security barricades.
record.consequences: Traders could not reach work; individual anticipated losses are not generalised.
record.record_type: Selective state blockade of international crossing access
record.relationship: Broader November 2019 informal-checkpoint restrictions are retained as a linked lead rather than assumed identical in scope.
record.status_observation: Historical evidence only; current status not inferred
record.official_rationale: Prevent the planned return of opposition leaders, which the government characterised as an attempted coup.
record.context: VOA reporters documented ordinary residents being stopped at approaches to the gate. Reuters separately quoted a police spokesperson claiming only alleged rebels would be stopped; this does not erase observed restrictions on ordinary traders.
record.uncertainty: Final lifting time was not recovered. The observed restrictions changed during the morning. This is a selective access blockade, not proof that all travellers or all Thai–Cambodian crossings were barred.
